listing.name: The Settlers / FreeSerf
listing.summary: Build a settlement in FreeSerf using your own DOS or Amiga game data.

steps.title: Choose data from your original game
steps.instruction: Use your original DOS data file SPAE.PA, SPAD.PA, SPAF.PA or SPAU.PA, or the six original Amiga files listed in the upstream guide. Copy them to ~/.local/share/freeserf on Linux or Mac, or to the freeserf folder under %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, and keep your originals separate. When launching from a terminal, -g takes the directory containing your data.

steps.title: Install the Windows or Mac release
steps.instruction: On Windows x64, use the Release installer. On Apple Silicon with macOS 26 or later, copy FreeSerf.app from the DMG. Set up your original data before opening the player.

steps.title: Keep your saves and settings
steps.instruction: FreeSerf keeps saves, including Ctrl+Z quicksaves and the optional autosave, in freeserf/saves under XDG_DATA_HOME on Linux, or in ~/freeserf/saves when XDG_DATA_HOME is unset. On Windows it uses the freeserf folder in your Saved Games folder, and on Mac Library/Application Support/freeserf/saves. Settings are in freeserf.ini: in ~/.local/share/freeserf or under XDG_DATA_HOME on Linux, in %APPDATA%\freeserf on Windows, and in Library/Application Support/freeserf on Mac. These stay in place when the player is replaced. Use -l with a saved game file to reopen it.

warnings: The v0.5 Mac DMG requires Apple Silicon. The publisher does not provide an Intel Mac or Android package in this release.

presentation.manual_preparation: Before first Play, copy your original DOS data file (SPAE.PA, SPAD.PA, SPAF.PA or SPAU.PA) or the six original Amiga files to ~/.local/share/freeserf, or to freeserf under XDG_DATA_HOME, not into Portcove's install folder, and keep your originals separate. Without them FreeSerf shows Could not find the game data. The package is the GPL-3 engine with a GPL-2 SoundFont and contains no game data. The Linux x86-64 player needs glibc 2.38 and a matching C++ runtime, for example Ubuntu 24.04 or later. FreeSerf keeps saves, including Ctrl+Z quicksaves and the optional autosave, in freeserf/saves under XDG_DATA_HOME or, when that is unset, in ~/freeserf/saves. Settings are in freeserf.ini in ~/.local/share/freeserf or under XDG_DATA_HOME. Those stay outside the managed copy, so Portcove neither backs them up nor removes them, and rollback does not rewind them. Portcove replaces the engine; you own the original data, saves and settings.
